step_by_step_reasoning:
1) Inventory: I kept all 10 entities from the world model. CloudFormation stays because a ledger arrow (CloudFormation -> EC2 Top) uses it, and ledger edges and their endpoints cannot be pruned. In the audio, CloudFormation is a deployment tool (about 40 YAML templates), so its edge is typed as 'control'.
2) EC2 fusion decision: I kept the three EC2 nodes separate. The audio says each Availability Zone (AZ) in us-east-1 runs 10 channels, and the whiteboard writes '10' next to each instance. So each icon stands for a separate AZ deployment that provides redundancy, not one icon drawn three times. Keeping them separate also keeps the ledger edges one-to-one.
3) ASG: This node has no arrow on the board. The audio says the primary and backup EC2 instances 'are supported also with auto scaling groups', so I added 3 control edges from ASG to the EC2 nodes. This keeps ASG from being an orphan node.
4) Third-party/on-premises nodes: NYC Satellite (the Hudson Yards business continuity, or BCP, uplink), ATL Satellite (the Atlanta uplink to affiliates) and TWD/CNN Center (Techwood/CNN Center site where Linear Ops quality-checks master files) all use the ThirdParty service type.
5) Flows:
 - Flow 0, main playout: TWD/CNN Center -> S3 (master files sent with Aspera, which the transcript calls 'Spera') -> EC2 x3 (parallel; Evertz Mediator registers the files, then they move to the ORT running on each instance) -> Direct Connect (x3 parallel; playout sent back on-premises as unicast over Evertz CloudBridge) -> TWD/CNN Center (the 'X chain', a tertiary path to air) -> ATL Satellite (compressed and uplinked to affiliates).
 - Flow 1, BCP: Direct Connect -> NYC Satellite (Hudson Yards, 8 channels).
 - Flow 2, deployment: CloudFormation -> EC2 Top.
 - Flow 3, scaling: ASG -> EC2 x3.
6) Self-check: The world model has 11 visual_connections entries. I emitted 14 edges: all 11 ledger edges plus 3 ASG control edges grounded in the audio. 14 >= 11.

graph.name: WarnerMedia HBO Cloud Linear Playout
graph.categories: Media & Entertainment, Broadcast Playout, Hybrid Cloud, Business Continuity
graph.notes: This cloud linear playout runs 30 channels in AWS us-east-1, with 10 channels per AZ and a primary and backup for each channel. It started as a business continuity (BCP) solution. It uses Evertz Mediator, ORT and Playtime software on EC2. Evertz CloudBridge runs at each end of the connection: in AWS, New York and Atlanta. The goal is five-nines availability. The deployment is repeatable through about 40 CloudFormation YAML templates. Future plans include live venue switching on the ORT and in-cloud multiplexing or compression handed directly to MVPDs.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores the master files for all brands. Files arrive from Atlanta through Aspera and are registered in Evertz Mediator.

nodes.notes: Auto Scaling groups support the primary and backup EC2 instances for each channel.

nodes.notes: One AZ in us-east-1 runs Evertz ORT/Playtime for 10 channels (primary and backup). Redundant with the other AZs.

nodes.name: Direct Connect
nodes.notes: Carries the playout back on-premises as a unicast signal over Evertz CloudBridge, which is installed at each end of the connection.

nodes.name: NYC Satellite
nodes.notes: Hudson Yards BCP uplink for 8 channels. Runs CloudBridge in New York.

nodes.name: ATL Satellite
nodes.notes: Atlanta uplink that distributes channels to affiliates.

nodes.name: TWD/CNN Center
nodes.notes: Techwood/CNN Center site. Linear Ops quality-checks master files here. An auto changeover switch chooses between Techwood, CNN Center and cloud playout. The signal is compressed here before uplink. Runs CloudBridge in Atlanta.
